outcome: stopping breastfeeding due to breast problems
cohort: The study included 150 women (50 with high-risk pregnancies and 100 with normal pregnancies) recruited from immunization and outpatient clinics at Sohag General Hospital.
finding: Women with high-risk pregnancies demonstrated significantly lower rates of breastfeeding initiation and exclusive breastfeeding, less skin-to-skin contact, and higher rates of lactation problems and formula feeding compared to women with normal pregnancies.
